text:
Your gaze seems veiled in vapor;

Your mysterious look—is it blue, gray, or green?—

By turns tender, cruel, dreamlike,

reflects the sky’s indolence and pallor.


You recall the white, warm, veiled days

that make captive souls dissolve in tears,

when, seized by a confused evil that strains them,

excited nerves mock the sleeper.


At times you resemble those lovely landscapes

that suns of misty seasons light…

And how you shine, O wet landscape

through which rays pass amid a veil of fog!


O dangerous woman, O seductive climates!

Shall I end by worshiping your snows and frosts,

and at last draw from implacable winter

pleasures sharper than ice and the sword?

translation.title: Cloudy Sky
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original; the sustained address and questions remain.
